outcome: Adherence to Institute of Medicine (IOM) gestational weight gain recommendations
cohort: 71 women with a history of gastric bypass and a singleton pregnancy, presenting at Odense University Hospital, Denmark, between November 2007 and October 2013
finding: The majority of pregnant women with gastric bypass did not fulfill guidelines for gestational weight gain, and while women who conceived later (≥18 months) after gastric bypass had a significantly higher risk of cesarean section and intravenous iron supplementation, early conception was not significantly associated with insufficient gestational weight gain, preterm delivery, or birthweight.
mod_finding: Women who conceived ≥18 months following gastric bypass had a significantly higher risk of requiring cesarean section or receiving intravenous iron supplementation compared to women who conceived <18 months after surgery.
